subject: Re: Confirmation of 'no training' commitment & retention details
messages:
From: Aditi Rao <aditi.rao@deltacorp.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@deltacorp.com, procurement@deltacorp.com
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions: training usage & retention wording

Sean —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security/legal team has a couple of targeted questions before we proceed to procurement:

1) We require an explicit commitment that customer data submitted via API or uploaded files will not be used to train or improve Redwood models. Can you confirm the exact language you put in customer contracts?

2) Please describe retention windows for:
   - Input data and request logs
   - KV/cache contents (if applicable)
   - Backups and snapshots

3) What is the deletion workflow? If DeltaCorp asks for deletion, how long until data is purged from primary systems and from backups?

We appreciate any written artifacts you can share (sample clause, playbook, SOC2 artifacts).

Thanks,
Aditi Rao
Security Programs Manager
DeltaCorp
[signature]

From: sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
To: Aditi Rao <aditi.rao@deltacorp.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions: training usage & retention wording

Aditi —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

• "No training" by default: Redwood does not use customer-provided data from API requests, uploaded files, or logs to train or improve our public models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a program we describe and contractually document.

• Retention: default retention windows are configurable but our hosted default is 30 days for request payloads and 90 days for aggregated logs/metrics. KV/cache entries are ephemeral and tied to session lifetimes; they are not persisted for model training.

• Deletion workflow: requests open a deletion ticket, primary data is purged within the configured SLA (we typically offer a 30-day purge for hosted accounts), and backups are scheduled for rotation — final purge from backups depends on backup cycle but we document the maximum exposure window per account.

I attached a short one-pager and a playbook that should help. For enterprise contracts we provide a sample "No-Training" clause and can add delta-specific wording. If you need the language inserted into the MSA, point me to the procurement contact and I’ll loop in legal.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_Security_OnePager.pdf (1 page)], [Attachment: data_deletion_playbook.pdf (6 pages)]

Best,

Thanks Sean — that helps. A couple follow-ups from our security lead:

• We need clarity on backup retention: if primary data is purged in 30 days, can you provide the maximum timeframe for backups to be overwritten or destroyed? Are backups encrypted separately with customer-specific keys for enterprise/private deployments?

Aditi

From: sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
To: Aditi Rao <aditi.rao@deltacorp.com>, procurement@deltacorp.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions: training usage & retention wording

Aditi,

Addressing the two bullets in order:

• Monitoring telemetry: technical telemetry (traces, error logs) is collected separately from customer payloads and is used only for service health and debugging. That telemetry is redacted/aggregated prior to any product analytics and is not included in any model training datasets. For customers with heightened needs we support telemetry redaction and dedicated logging sinks in Private/Dedicated deployments.

• Backups: hosted account backups follow a 90 day retention cycle by default; we can commit to a maximum window for your account in contract (for example, 90 days) and we offer shorter windows for enterprise configurations. For Private engagements we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), which gives you control over backup decryption.

• Doc/Clause: I attached a sample "no train" clause as a Word doc. If you confirm the language we'll send it through DocuSign; procurement can pre-sign.

Attachments: [Attachment: sample_no_train_clause.docx]

Operational notes (for transparency): when a deletion request is submitted we: 1) mark the customer data tombstoned in the primary store; 2) remove indexes and references within 24–72 hours; 3) trigger backend jobs that purge the blobs within the SLA window; 4) schedule backup rotations — depending on the backup cadence final removal from cold backups could occur up to the agreed maximum window. We keep an audit trail for deletion requests and can provide timestamps on completion.

Looping in Karithik (ops/legal coverage) to confirm contract wording and SOC2 artifacts.

Best,
Sean
